title: Per-user install foundation
objective: Deliver the per-user install foundation defined in docs/canonical/P12_INSTALLER_LIFECYCLE_DESIGN.md sections 3 through 5: a release manifest format with fail-closed verification, a packaging script that produces it, and a human-invoked `cotra` CLI with `install`, `uninstall`, and `version` that installs verified payloads under the protected Cotra state root with an owner-only protected DACL, an atomic version pointer, an optional user PATH entry, and uninstall that separates removable executable state from retained user data.

include: a new cotra-lifecycle crate providing the `cotra` binary with install, uninstall, version, and help commands, human and --json output, and typed exit codes

release manifest schema cotra-release-manifest-v1 with version, configuration schema range, and per-file relative path, size, and SHA-256, rejecting unknown fields, duplicate case-insensitive paths, hostile paths (absolute, drive, UNC, stream, relative segments, reserved device names, forbidden characters, trailing dot or space, non-ASCII), missing required files, unlisted files, links, and reparse points

prerequisite validation that fails closed: Windows build 17763 or later, no avoidable elevation (a UAC split-token administrator running elevated is refused; systems without a split token cannot drop elevation and proceed), and Node.js 20 or later verified by actually running it

install under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Cotra only: refuse a link or non-directory root, apply and read back an owner-only protected DACL granting only the current user and SYSTEM with descendants reset to inherit, stage into a per-install staging directory, re-verify the copy, activate as versions\<version>, write current.json and install.json atomically, and replace bin\cotra.exe by renaming any running copy aside
same-version reinstall repairs a tampered or missing payload; installing a different version over an existing install is refused as a conflict until the update grain
optional user PATH entry in HKCU\Environment, added once, recorded, removed exactly on uninstall, with the environment-change broadcast

uninstall that refuses while a supervisor record exists, removes versions, bin, the pointer, the install record, run state, and the recorded PATH entry, relocates a running cotra.exe from the install root to the temp directory, retains and reports configuration, secrets, logs, and audit, approval, trust, and browser-profile history by default, and purges them only with --purge-data --yes
every destructive operation guarded to paths strictly beneath the install root
scripts/package-release.mjs producing a release directory and manifest from a release build
Windows-native tests on real ACLs, a real registry PATH value under an isolated test key, and the real `cotra` binary installing from a synthetic release into an isolated LOCALAPPDATA
a design-document amendment recording the avoidable-elevation rule
exclude: any MCP tool, agent capability, provider operation, or approval change
start, stop, status, doctor, supervisor, tunnel setup, workspace configuration, or cotra-mcp-host, which belong to the lifecycle runtime grain
update, rollback, recovery, and the release workflow, which belong to the update grain
service installation, scheduled tasks, machine-wide installation, or requesting elevation
writes outside %LOCALAPPDATA%\Cotra other than the recorded HKCU PATH value and the relocated running CLI in the temp directory

authority_delta.filesystem: The human-invoked CLI writes only beneath %LOCALAPPDATA%\Cotra (plus relocating its own running executable to the temp directory on uninstall). No agent filesystem authority is added; SG-000041 keeps the install root outside every admitted workspace.
authority_delta.process: The CLI runs the configured Node.js executable with --version only. No agent process authority is added.
authority_delta.secrets: No secret is read or written. Install and uninstall output contain paths and versions only.
authority_delta.privileged: None. No elevation is requested; avoidable elevation is refused; no service or scheduled task is created.

invariants: no payload file is copied before the whole release verifies, and no version is activated before its copy re-verifies
the version pointer references only verified versions and is replaced atomically
the install root carries a protected DACL granting only the current user and SYSTEM, verified by read-back, and ACL failures abort
destructive operations act only strictly beneath the install root
uninstall never removes retained user data without --purge-data --yes and never touches workspaces
the lifecycle CLI is not reachable from MCP and adds no agent capability

acceptance.claim: Tests prove manifest verification rejects tampered, unlisted, missing-required, duplicate, unknown-field, wrong-schema, hostile-path, link, and reparse-point releases.
Tests prove prerequisites fail closed on old Windows builds, avoidable elevation, missing Node.js, and Node.js older than 20, before any write.
Tests prove install stages, re-verifies, activates, writes atomic records, and leaves no staging residue, and that a tampered release installs nothing.
Windows-native tests prove the protected DACL is applied, foreign explicit entries on descendants are reset, and verification detects a foreign principal added afterwards.
Windows-native tests prove the user PATH entry is added once and removed exactly under an isolated registry key.
Tests prove same-version reinstall repairs a tampered payload and a different version is refused.
Tests prove uninstall retains user data by default, purges only with confirmation, refuses while a supervisor record exists, and guards every removal to paths beneath the install root.
A Windows-native test runs the real `cotra` binary to refuse a tampered release, install from an extracted release, run the installed CLI, repair, uninstall with retention, and purge.
All closed SG-000001 through SG-000041 regressions pass unchanged.

Exact-head Windows and Ubuntu Rust, Node, Governance, genuine TypeSafe Jev, Alibaba Open Code Review, exact-diff security review, manual review of excluded files, and zero unresolved blocking review threads all pass.

successor_requirements.p12_lifecycle: The lifecycle runtime grain adds cotra-mcp-host, tunnel setup, workspace configuration, start, stop, status, and doctor, and extends uninstall to stop a running instance with verified termination.
successor_requirements.p12_update: The update grain adds update, rollback, failed-update recovery, the release workflow, and a CI job that installs from a packaged artifact.

done_when: The per-user install foundation is specified: verified manifest-based install, protected per-user layout, atomic pointer, optional PATH entry, and retention-aware uninstall through a human-invoked CLI with no agent authority.
